title: Powerful Integers
summary: Given three integers x, y, and bound, return a list of all powerful integers that are less than or equal to bound.
statement: Given three integers x, y, and bound, return a list of all powerful integers that are less than or equal to bound. A powerful integer is defined as one that can be represented as x^i + y^j where i and j are non-negative integers. Each value in the output list should appear at most once.
constraints: Return distinct values x^i+y^j <= bound for nonnegative i,j.
Output order is irrelevant; x or y may equal one.
hints: Enumerate geometric powers of x and y, but guard bases equal to one.
Use nested loops over powers and a set for duplicate sums.
Break a power loop after its base-one iteration; otherwise multiply by the base.
Every exponent pair appears once in the loops and the bound makes both finite.
editorial: Every exponent pair appears once in the loops and the bound makes both finite.
